National Knowledge and Research Center for Emergency Readiness (Haifa University / NEMA) (https://geo.haifa.ac.il/~inbar/)

jerusalem_district_specific_assessment.geography: Judean Mountains, Elevation 600m - 850m above sea level, Mediterranean to semi-arid transitional climate zone.

top_hazards.historical_benchmark: Dec 2013 Storm Alexa (50-70 cm snow, 40,000 homes blacked out, Route 1 closed 72h).
top_hazards.vulnerability_factors: Mountain topography, reliance on two major highway lifelines (Route 1 & Route 443), above-ground power grid vulnerable to snow and branch collapse.

top_hazards.historical_benchmark: August 2021 Wildfire (25,000 dunams burned, 2,000 evacuated, hospital evacuated).
top_hazards.vulnerability_factors: Dense pine forests planted during 20th century bordering residential suburban communities, steep topography creating chimney wind effects, frequent Sharav wind conditions.

top_hazards.historical_benchmark: 1927 Jericho M 6.3 Earthquake (> 130 dead in Jerusalem/Nablus, Mount of Olives and Augusta Victoria heavily damaged).
top_hazards.vulnerability_factors: Proximity to Dead Sea fault (~25-30 km east), large inventory of unreinforced masonry buildings built before Israeli Standard SI 413 (pre-1980), high density in Old City and East Jerusalem.

top_hazards.historical_benchmark: Sept 2020 Record Heatwave (42.7°C, all-time record night minimum 31.5°C).
top_hazards.vulnerability_factors: Rapid urban densification, limestone paving and stone facades retaining nocturnal heat, vulnerable elderly population.

top_hazards.hazard: Urban Flash Floods & Downstream Desert Surges
top_hazards.historical_benchmark: April 2018 Nahal Tzafit disaster; January 2020 valley inundations.
top_hazards.vulnerability_factors: Steep runoff gradients flowing east into Judean desert wadis; narrow ravines and drainage pinch-points in valley bottoms (Nahal Sorek, Kidron).

Coastal Flood.description: Winter storm surges and sea-level rise impacting low-lying Mediterranean coastal areas.

Earthquake.description: Greater than 10% chance of potentially damaging ground shaking (> VII MMI) in the next 50 years along the Dead Sea Transform boundary.

Extreme Heat.description: Prolonged exposure to extreme thermal stress. Summer heatwaves (Sharav/Khamsin) reaching 40-45°C in mountains and > 48°C in rift valley.

Geotechnical Sinkholes.description: Sudden subsurface collapse due to salt dissolution (> 7,000 sinkholes along Dead Sea coast) and karst voids beneath Jerusalem's limestone bedrock.

Landslide.description: Moderate potential for slope failure, rockfalls, and soil slips along steep mountain canyons in Judean Hills and Galilee during high-saturation winter storms.

River Flood.description: Potentially-damaging and life-threatening river and wadi flash floods are expected to occur at least once in the next 10 years.

Tsunami.description: Mediterranean seismic or submarine landslide triggered tsunami waves (0.5m - 3m) and Dead Sea internal seiche waves documented historically.

Urban Flood.description: Surface water accumulation during high-intensity cloudbursts due to high impervious surface ratios in urbanized municipalities like Jerusalem and Tel Aviv.
Urban Flood.source: ThinkHazard! (https://thinkhazard.org/) / Jerusalem Institute for Policy Research (https://jerusaleminstitute.org.il/)

Water Scarcity & Drought.description: High baseline water stress with severe multi-year droughts occurring every 10-15 years. Mitigated through national desalination infrastructure.

Wildfire.description: Greater than 50% chance of encountering weather conducive to massive wildfires in any given year. Climate change projected to intensify fire season length and fuel aridity.
